notes: Identical to data/lsptest/campaigns/main_v1.json except id, description, corpus, eligibility, project overrides and these notes, so that the two corpora are two runs of one campaign design.
The signature cap is per campaign: signatures confirmed in main_v1 are not capped here; groups that repeat a main_v1 bug are matched to its cause when the groups are judged.
Eligibility and project overrides are decided from the corpus probe (data/lsptest/corpus_v2_prepared.md) before the run, and recorded here.

main_v1's notes on seeds, oracle options and cost controls apply unchanged: race0 and race200 use seed 1, the seed of the first settled run: same targets and histories, different timing, so that timing-only violations can be told apart. | r3_routes, r6_crossimpl and r0_crash do not use max_cases (they check every target). | server_limits: at most 2 rust-analyzer runs at a time (a session takes up to 3.5 GB; R1 runs two side by side). | Cost controls (campaign_costs.py): candidates with a registered legitimate-difference label (r3_routes definitionConsistency.signature / .shorthand) are recorded as labelled-legitimate without replay; a signature confirmed in 3 runs is capped (later candidates recorded as capped, not replayed).

Eligibility (2026-11-18, from data/lsptest/corpus_v2_prepared.md): all 50 probes settled. Dependencies failed in the frozen preparation for four TypeScript projects; three were installed by hand under the frozen pipeline's own rule (the project's package manager, no install scripts) and are forced above. colinhacks/zod stays out by the eligibility rule (deps failed): its package.json pins the package manager nub@0.8.3, which is not on the npm registry, and its lockfile is rejected by pnpm 10 (no entry for the workspace package) and by npm (workspace: protocol). So 48 of the 50 pairs run.
